{
  "verdict": "needs-attention",
  "summary": "Do not ship: batching violates the API cap, quota validation accepts the forbidden boundary, and the memory claim is false. All five existing tests pass despite these defects.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Batches exceed the API's 256-record cap",
      "body": "The hard-coded 265 emits rejected batches: range(257) produces one 257-record batch; range(1000) produces lengths [265, 265, 265, 205]. Existing tests check counts without enforcing the per-batch limit.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py",
      "line_start": 18,
      "line_end": 18,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Use API_BATCH_LIMIT for both slicing and stride. Test 256, 257, and larger inputs, asserting every batch contains at most 256 records and preserves input order."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Quota validation accepts a forbidden 10% reserve",
      "body": "For [0.3, 0.3, 0.3], floating-point rounding produces reserve 0.10000000000000009, so an intended 90% allocation passes. The test explicitly requires this incorrect acceptance. The same guard also returns NaN for [float('nan')], although NaN is not strictly above 10%.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py",
      "line_start": 24,
      "line_end": 27,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Define exact quota arithmetic using integer units or decimal semantics, reject non-finite values, and test rejection at exactly 10%, below it, and for NaN. Change the three-equal-shares test to expect ValueError."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "The documented memory profile contradicts eager allocation",
      "body": "make_batches materializes the entire input and every output batch simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with ten million repeated None records peaked at 162,423,328 bytes, contradicting the under-4-MB claim even without allocating record payloads. Callers relying on the documented bound risk exhausting memory.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py",
      "line_start": 7,
      "line_end": 8,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Document the actual O(n) memory behavior and reproducible measurement conditions, or implement incremental batch generation and remeasure before claiming bounded memory."
    }
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Fix the batch cap and quota arithmetic, add boundary and rejection tests, and correct or substantiate the memory profile."
  ]
}

result.summary: Do not ship: batching violates the API cap, quota validation accepts the forbidden boundary, and the memory claim is false. All five existing tests pass despite these defects.

findings.title: Batches exceed the API's 256-record cap
findings.body: The hard-coded 265 emits rejected batches: range(257) produces one 257-record batch; range(1000) produces lengths [265, 265, 265, 205]. Existing tests check counts without enforcing the per-batch limit.
findings.recommendation: Use API_BATCH_LIMIT for both slicing and stride. Test 256, 257, and larger inputs, asserting every batch contains at most 256 records and preserves input order.

findings.title: Quota validation accepts a forbidden 10% reserve
findings.body: For [0.3, 0.3, 0.3], floating-point rounding produces reserve 0.10000000000000009, so an intended 90% allocation passes. The test explicitly requires this incorrect acceptance. The same guard also returns NaN for [float('nan')], although NaN is not strictly above 10%.
findings.recommendation: Define exact quota arithmetic using integer units or decimal semantics, reject non-finite values, and test rejection at exactly 10%, below it, and for NaN. Change the three-equal-shares test to expect ValueError.

findings.title: The documented memory profile contradicts eager allocation
findings.body: make_batches materializes the entire input and every output batch simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with ten million repeated None records peaked at 162,423,328 bytes, contradicting the under-4-MB claim even without allocating record payloads. Callers relying on the documented bound risk exhausting memory.
findings.recommendation: Document the actual O(n) memory behavior and reproducible measurement conditions, or implement incremental batch generation and remeasure before claiming bounded memory.

next_steps: Fix the batch cap and quota arithmetic, add boundary and rejection tests, and correct or substantiate the memory profile.
